review_unsupported_claims: Rationale says the policy addresses data quality standards and testing, which is true, but it does not note that 4.3.1 'დროულობის' (timeliness) is a data-quality dimension that touches the topic.
review_comment: 4.3.1 lists 'დროულობის' (timeliness) as a data-quality requirement, but nothing requires control or elimination of outdated data whose trend no longer matches current conditions ('მოძველებული მონაცემების ... კონტროლი და აღმოფხვრა'). Timeliness is only a loose neighbour, so 'none' is defensible, and it fits the gold gap (no Art. 9¹ content at all).

review_unsupported_claims: The evidence quote for §7.1.3 is empty („“) and cannot be verified. The finding says detailed 'technical and procedural' requirements for validating purchased models are missing, but the regulation only requires the policy to describe the necessary requirements, and 7.1.3 refers to Chapter 5, which contains them.
review_comment: 7.1.3 says 'შეძენილი მოდელის შიდა ვალიდაცია ტარდება ამ პოლიტიკის მე-5 თავის შესაბამისად. ვალიდაცია შეიძლება შესრულდეს ბანკის ვალიდაციის ჯგუფის ან დამოუკიდებელი მესამე მხარის მიერ', and 5.1.1 extends validation to purchased models. This describes both the internal and the third-party validation and the requirements, so the finding demands more than Art. 3(3). The proposal adds only a vague 'technical and procedural requirements' sentence.

review_unsupported_claims: Treats documentation as a missing component of risk assessment, but the document has no use-risk assessment at all (5.2.1 applies uniform validation), so 'partial' implies a risk-assessment process that does not exist.
review_comment: The regulation lists documentation as a component of model-use risk assessment inside the ranking methodology. The document has no ranking or use-risk assessment (5.2.1 'ერთიანი მეთოდოლოგიით ... მიუხედავად მოდელის ტიპისა და დანიშნულებისა'), so this sub-item is absent, not partially met. The quoted 4.2.1 and 5.3.2 are real but concern development and verification, and the proposal bolts a sentence onto the development clause 4.2.1, which is the wrong place.

review_unsupported_claims: Cites only 4.4.1 and misses 5.3.3, which covers ongoing monitoring and benchmark comparison; the claim that no trigger on new information exists is largely true.
review_comment: Clause 4.4.1 'ამოწმებს მოდელის სიზუსტეს ... მგრძნობელობას' and 5.3.1 run sensitivity tests, and 5.3.3 requires quarterly monitoring, but nothing requires re-running the development-stage tests 'ახალი ინფორმაციის მიღებისას'. Partial fits, though the gold gaps on this article (replication, override justification) are different problems.

review_unsupported_claims: Evidence for §10.1 is an empty quote („“). The finding says 10.1 does not mention documentation of build/validation/update, but 10.1 does cover 'დოკუმენტაციის სისრულე' and 'მოდელის გამოყენებისა და შიდა ვალიდაციის პროცესებს'.
review_comment: Clause 10.1 has internal audit assess 'დოკუმენტაციის სისრულე', which covers documentation generally, but it does not name the build, validation and update processes. The second sentence of Art. 7(2), assessing operating systems and data management, is not in the obligation or the document. Partial is reasonable and the proposal targets the gap.

review_unsupported_claims: Says the document lacks the 'all three lines positive assessment' condition; 4.5.1 requires the validation conclusion and committee consent but not first- or third-line sign-off. It misses the real defect: the approver is not independent of the lines. Also the obligation omits the senior-management rule for supervisory models, though 8.1 gives the directorate that role.
review_comment: Under 3.3.1 the committee is chaired by the CRO (second line) and includes the head of RAMD, which houses the validation team (3.5.1), so approval under 4.5.1 'მოდელების კომიტეტის თანხმობის შემდეგ' comes from a body inside the lines of defence, which conflicts with 'დაცვის ხაზებისაგან დამოუკიდებელმა'. The system flagged 'partial' for missing qualifications and sign-offs and did not see this conflict; the proposal keeps the CRO-led committee, so it does not fix the independence defect.

review_unsupported_claims: The finding claims the regulation requires the third party to decide suitability. The text 'უნდა განისაზღვროს' is passive: it does not say who decides, and its logic ('ამის შემდეგ') points to the model user. The proposal would impose a duty on the vendor that the regulation does not impose.
review_comment: The regulation says 'ამის შემდეგ უნდა განისაზღვროს, არის თუ არა მოდელი ... მიზანშეწონილი' with no named actor, and clause 7.1.2 'მოწოდებული ინფორმაციის საფუძველზე ბანკი იღებს გადაწყვეტილებას, შეესაბამება თუ არა მოდელი ბანკის პროდუქტებს' matches it. The finding misread the passive voice and calls compliance a gap; the real gaps on this article (own-data testing, vendor test results) are untouched.

review_unsupported_claims: Cites only 7.1.1 and misses 7.1.3 and 5.1.1 (validation of purchased models), though neither applies a risk-based approach; 'partial' implies some risk-based review exists.
review_comment: Nothing in the document requires a risk-based review of purchased models; 7.1.3 applies the Chapter 5 validation, which per 5.2.1 is uniform ('მიუხედავად მოდელის ტიპისა და დანიშნულებისა'), the opposite of a risk-based approach. 7.1.1 gives ownership only. The gap matches the gold (no risk-based review of purchased models), so 'none' is better than 'partial'.
